errors.t212Unauthorized: Trading 212 did not accept the key and secret. Check you copied both (the secret is shown only once), or generate a new key and update the credentials.
errors.t212Forbidden: The key is missing a read permission. Generate a new key with Account data, Metadata, Portfolio and History switched on (see step 3 of the guide).
errors.t212RateLimited: Trading 212 is rate-limiting requests. Nothing to do — the next sync retries automatically.
errors.ibkrExpired: The Flex token has expired. Generate a new one in Client Portal and update the credentials with its new expiry date.
errors.ibkrIp: The Flex token is restricted to a different IP address. Update the IP in Flex Web Service Configuration or generate a token without IP restriction.
errors.ibkrQueryId: IBKR does not recognise the query ID. Use the number shown next to your Activity Flex Query.
errors.ibkrToken: IBKR does not recognise the token. Copy it again from Flex Web Service Configuration (a new token invalidates the old one).
errors.ibkrNoStatement: IBKR has no statement for this account yet (error 1003). Check that the Query ID is the number of your Activity Flex Query, with Period "Last 365 Calendar Days", and that the account already has activity.
errors.ibkrLocked: IBKR temporarily blocked the token after too many failed attempts (error 1025). Automatic syncs pause for 12 hours — don't press Sync meanwhile, it extends the block. If it persists, generate a new Flex token and update the connection.
errors.binanceNotReadOnly: This Binance key can trade, transfer or withdraw, so it was refused. Create a new API key with only "Enable Reading" ticked and update the credentials.
errors.binanceNoReading: This Binance key cannot read the account. Edit it in API Management and tick "Enable Reading".
errors.binanceUnauthorized: Binance did not accept the key: check the API Key and Secret Key, and that this server's IP is on the key's list of trusted IPs.
errors.binanceRateLimited: Binance is rate-limiting requests. Nothing to do — the next sync retries automatically.
errors.binanceClock: Binance rejected the request time. Check that this computer's clock is synchronised.

guide.title: How to connect
guide.subtitle: Step-by-step: create read-only credentials at your broker and paste them here.
guide.security: This app only calls the brokers' read endpoints and blocks anything else before a request leaves your server. Credentials are stored encrypted on your server, never shown again, never logged and never shared with AI clients.

t212.intro: Trading 212 has no "log in with Trading 212" option: you create an API key in the app. Each key covers one account (Invest or Stocks ISA — CFD and SIPP are not supported).

1.title: Open Trading 212 on the right account
1.body: In the app or on the web, switch to the Invest or Stocks ISA account you want to track.

2.title: Open the API settings
2.body: Go to Menu (☰) → Settings → API (Beta), accept the risk warning and tap Generate API key. Name it e.g. personal-finance.

3.title: Choose read-only permissions
3.body: Switch on only what the app reads. Anything that places orders or edits pies must stay off — the app would never use it, but a leaked key could.

4.title: Restrict the IP (recommended)
4.body: Choose Restrict access to trusted IPs and enter your server's public IP. Pick Unrestricted only if that IP changes often.

5.title: Copy the key and the secret
5.body: Tap Generate. You get an API key and an API secret — the secret is shown only once, so copy both now.

6.title: Paste them here
6.body: Paste the key and secret in the form below, keep Live and save. The first sync starts right away; if something is wrong the card tells you what to fix.

on.2: Metadata — instrument names, ISIN, ETF or stock

t212.revoke: Revoke anytime: Trading 212 → Settings → API (Beta) → select the key → Delete. The key stops working immediately.
t212.csv: The API has no valuation history and no dividend withholding tax. Export your history (Trading 212 → History → Export, CSV) and use Import CSV on the connection card to backfill older data — duplicates are ignored. Without any key you can still record trades by hand in Portfolio.

ibkr.intro: IBKR only offers OAuth to approved companies, so individual accounts connect through the Flex Web Service: a report (Flex Query) plus a token. It is reporting-only — it cannot trade.

1.title: Open Flex Queries
1.body: Log in to Client Portal and go to Performance & Reports → Flex Queries.

2.title: Create an Activity Flex Query
2.body: Next to Activity Flex Query click + and name it e.g. personal-finance.

3.title: Tick these sections
3.body: In each section choose Select All fields (simplest), with the option shown in brackets.

4.title: Set the delivery configuration
4.body: Format XML · Period Last 365 Calendar Days · Date format yyyyMMdd · Time format HHmmss · Date/time separator ; (semicolon). Save and confirm.

5.title: Note the Query ID
5.body: Back in the list, the Query ID is the number shown for your query (use the info icon if it is hidden).

6.title: Generate the Flex token
6.body: On the same page open Flex Web Service Configuration (gear icon), enable it and click Generate A New Token. Pick the expiry (up to 1 year), optionally restrict it to your server's IP, and copy the token.

7.title: Paste them here
7.body: Paste the token and the query ID in the form below and enter the token's expiry date. The first sync backfills several years and can take a few minutes.

on.4: Cash Transactions (Detail) — deposits, dividends, withholding tax, fees, interest
on.7: Net Asset Value (NAV) in Base — daily value history

ibkr.revoke: Revoke anytime: Flex Web Service Configuration → Generate A New Token (the old one stops working) or switch the service off.
ibkr.csv: IBKR has no CSV import here — the Flex query already delivers the full history. Without a token you can still record trades by hand in Portfolio.

binance.intro: Binance connects with an API key that can only read. Before every sync the app asks Binance what the key is allowed to do and refuses it if it could trade, transfer or withdraw.

1.title: Make sure API keys are available
1.body: Binance only creates API keys on a verified account with two-factor authentication on. Use the website (binance.com) — it is easier than the app for this.

2.title: Create the key
2.body: Go to Profile → Account → API Management → Create API, choose System generated, name it e.g. personal-finance and confirm with 2FA.

3.title: Leave only reading on
3.body: Click Edit restrictions. Keep Enable Reading ticked and everything else off. A key with any other permission is refused by the app.

4.title: Restrict it to your IP
4.body: Choose Restrict access to trusted IPs only and enter your server's public IP (on the server: curl -4 ifconfig.me). Save — Binance asks for 2FA again.

5.title: Copy the API Key and the Secret Key
5.body: The Secret Key is shown only once, right after creating the key. Copy both now; if you lose the secret, delete the key and create another.

6.title: Paste them here
6.body: Paste the API Key and the Secret Key in the form below and save. The first sync reads your spot and Earn balances and the last 180 days of Earn rewards.

on.1: Enable Reading — balances, Simple Earn positions and rewards, your fills (for the average price)

off.5: Futures, European Options and any other trading permission

binance.revoke: Revoke anytime: Binance → API Management → Delete next to the key. It stops working immediately.
binance.csv: There is no Binance file import. Coins on other exchanges or in a wallet can be added by hand in Portfolio → Add crypto; the same coin on Binance and by hand shows as one position.

ai.subtitle: Each AI client gets its own revocable token and explicit permissions. Reading is the default; writing is opt-in per client, and nothing can trade or move money.
ai.empty: No AI clients. Create one for Claude Code, ChatGPT or a local model.
ai.auditNote: Records what was asked and how much was returned — never the values.
ai.sensitive: Sensitive — off unless you really need them
ai.tokenOnce: Copy it now: it is shown only once and stored only as a hash. Anyone with this token can use the permitted data — and make the permitted changes.
ai.copyFailed: Copy failed — select the text manually.
ai.confirmDelete: Delete "{{name}}" permanently? Its token stops working immediately and it disappears from this list. Its audit history is kept.
ai.writeGroup: Write — the AI can change your data
ai.writeNote: Off unless you tick them. Each write changes one record, is audited and limited per hour; AI deletions go to the recycle bin for 30 days. Broker data is never writable.
ai.confirmWrite: Allow this client to change your data ({{scopes}})? Every write is audited, limited per hour and deletions stay restorable for 30 days. Only grant it to clients you trust, and ask your AI tool to confirm each write.
ai.recycleNote: What AI clients deleted. Restore with one click; items are deleted for good 30 days after deletion.

assistant.subtitle: Ask about your finances. Answers use the same permission-checked tools as MCP clients — read-only unless you grant the assistant a write permission under AI access.
assistant.enableHelp: It is optional. To enable it, set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in deploy/.env and restart. You can limit what it can read under AI access → In-app assistant.

assistant.privacy: Your question and only the minimal tool results are sent to {{model}} (Anthropic API). Conversations are not stored. Permissions: {{scopes}}.

loans.title: Loan
loans.subtitle: What you owe, when it ends and what early repayments would save.
loans.setupText: With the amount, rate and term, the app works out the instalment, what is left to pay, when it ends and how much interest you will still pay. The account's balance then follows the plan.
